title: Interfaces, inheritance, and composition
summary: Design seams in your code with contracts, and prefer composition when inheritance stops earning its keep.

workedExample.title: Refactor a conditional into polymorphism
steps: Identify the axis of change: the rendering format. Keep the stable data (`title`, `body`) as method parameters.
Define `ILessonRenderer` with `string Render(string title, string body)`.
Implement `PlainTextRenderer`, `HtmlRenderer`, and `MarkdownRenderer`. Each class owns exactly one format.
The caller receives an `ILessonRenderer` and calls `Render` without a conditional. Adding a format means adding a class, not editing existing branches.

Select the implementation once at composition time — for example in a factory or dependency-injection registration. The Open/Closed idea is a consequence, not the goal: the goal is local, understandable change.

explainPrompt: Explain the difference between an interface and an abstract class. Then describe a situation where composition is clearly better than inheritance.

checkQuestions.prompt: What can an abstract class do that a C# interface cannot (without default members)?
options: Store instance fields and share implementation
Be used as a parameter type
checkQuestions.explanation: Abstract classes can hold state and implementation. Interfaces traditionally declare contracts only, though default interface methods now allow limited implementation.
optionExplanations: Both can be implemented or derived by multiple types.
Both can be used as parameter types.

checkQuestions.prompt: Why is depending on an interface useful for testing?
options: It makes the program run faster
A fake implementation can replace real I/O in a test
It removes the need for constructors
checkQuestions.explanation: A contract allows substituting a test double, isolating the code under test from slow or unreliable dependencies.
optionExplanations: Interfaces do not inherently improve runtime speed.
Interfaces do not affect constructor requirements.
Interfaces have nothing to do with static methods.

checkQuestions.prompt: What is a sign that composition may be better than inheritance?
options: You want to reuse one method from a base class
The derived class is not genuinely a subtype and only needs some behavior
The base class has no methods
checkQuestions.explanation: Inheritance should model an is-a relationship with substitutability. Reusing a fragment of behavior is often better handled by a collaborator.
optionExplanations: Reusing one method is a common misuse of inheritance; a collaborator is usually cleaner.
An empty base class provides no reason for inheritance.
Abstract classes are one tool, not a goal.
